entries.name: Matrix.diag_mul_of_blockTriangular_id
entries.docstring:
For upper-triangular matrices, the diagonal of a product is the product of the diagonals.
This is a specific case of a more general property for block-triangular matrices.
entries.snippet:
lemma diag_mul_of_blockTriangular_id {A B : Matrix m m 𝕂}
    (hA : BlockTriangular A id) (hB : BlockTriangular B id) : (A * B).diag = A.diag * B.diag

entries.name: Matrix.blockTriangular.pow
entries.docstring: Powers of block triangular matrices are block triangular.
entries.snippet:
lemma blockTriangular.pow {A : Matrix m m 𝕂} (hA : BlockTriangular A id) (k : ℕ) :
    BlockTriangular (A ^ k) id

entries.name: Matrix.diag_pow_of_blockTriangular_id
entries.docstring: For an upper-triangular matrix, the diagonal of a power is the power of the diagonal.
entries.snippet:
lemma diag_pow_of_blockTriangular_id {A : Matrix m m 𝕂}
    (hA : BlockTriangular A id) (k : ℕ) : (A ^ k).diag = A.diag ^ k

entries.name: Matrix.blockTriangular_exp_of_blockTriangular_id

entries.snippet:
lemma blockTriangular_exp_of_blockTriangular_id
    {A : Matrix m m 𝕂} (hA : BlockTriangular A id) :
    (NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 A).BlockTriangular id

entries.name: Matrix.diag_pow_entry_eq_pow_diag_entry
entries.docstring:
For an upper–triangular matrix `A`, the `(i,i)` entry of the power `A ^ n`
is simply the `n`-th power of the original diagonal entry.

entries.name: Matrix.exp_series_diag_term_eq
entries.docstring:
Each term in the matrix exponential series equals the corresponding scalar term on the
diagonal
entries.snippet:
lemma exp_series_diag_term_eq {A : Matrix m m 𝕂} (hA : BlockTriangular A id)
    (n : ℕ) (i : m) :
    ((n.factorial : 𝕂)⁻¹ • (A ^ n)) i i = (n.factorial : 𝕂)⁻¹ • (A i i) ^ n

entries.name: Matrix.matrix_exp_series_diag_eq_scalar_series
entries.docstring: The diagonal of the matrix exponential series equals the scalar exponential series
entries.snippet:
lemma matrix_exp_series_diag_eq_scalar_series {A : Matrix m m 𝕂} (hA : BlockTriangular A id)
    (i : m) :
    (∑' n, ((n.factorial : 𝕂)⁻¹ • (A ^ n)) i i) = ∑' n, (n.factorial : 𝕂)⁻¹ • (A i i) ^ n

entries.name: Matrix.diag_exp_of_blockTriangular_id
entries.docstring:
The diagonal of the exponential of an upper-triangular matrix `A` consists of the
exponentials of the diagonal entries of `A`.
entries.snippet:
theorem diag_exp_of_blockTriangular_id
    {A : Matrix m m 𝕂} (hA : BlockTriangular A id) :
    (NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 A).diag = fun i => NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 (A i i)

entries.name: Matrix.det_exp_of_blockTriangular_id

entries.snippet:
lemma det_exp_of_blockTriangular_id {A : Matrix m m 𝕂} (hA : BlockTriangular A id) :
    (NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 A).det = NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 A.trace

entries.name: Matrix.trace_unitary_conj
entries.docstring: The trace is invariant under unitary conjugation.
entries.snippet:
lemma trace_unitary_conj (A : Matrix m m 𝕂) (U : unitaryGroup m 𝕂) :
    trace ((U : Matrix m m 𝕂) * A * star (U : Matrix m m 𝕂)) = trace A

entries.name: Matrix.det_unitary_conj
entries.docstring: The determinant is invariant under unitary conjugation.
entries.snippet:
lemma det_unitary_conj (A : Matrix m m 𝕂) (U : unitaryGroup m 𝕂) :
    det ((U : Matrix m m 𝕂) * A * star (U : Matrix m m 𝕂)) = det A

entries.name: Matrix.exp_unitary_conj
entries.docstring: The exponential of a matrix commutes with unitary conjugation.
entries.snippet:
lemma exp_unitary_conj (A : Matrix m m 𝕂) (U : unitaryGroup m 𝕂) :
    NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 ((U : Matrix m m 𝕂) * A * star (U : Matrix m m 𝕂)) =
      (U : Matrix m m 𝕂) * NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 A * star (U : Matrix m m 𝕂)

entries.name: Matrix.det_exp_unitary_conj
entries.snippet:
lemma det_exp_unitary_conj (A : Matrix m m 𝕂) (U : unitaryGroup m 𝕂) :
    (NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 ((U : Matrix m m 𝕂) * A * star (U : Matrix m m 𝕂))).det =
    (NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 A).det

entries.name: Matrix.det_exp
entries.docstring:
The determinant of the exponential of a matrix is the exponential of its trace.
This is also known as **Lie's trace formula**.
entries.snippet:
theorem det_exp {𝕂 m : Type*} [RCLike 𝕂] [IsAlgClosed 𝕂] [Fintype m] [LinearOrder m]
    (A : Matrix m m 𝕂) :
    (NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 A).det = NormedSpace.exp 𝕂 A.trace

entries.name: Matrix.map_tsum
entries.snippet:
lemma map_tsum {α β m n : Type*}
    [AddCommMonoid α] [AddCommMonoid β] [TopologicalSpace α] [TopologicalSpace β]
    [T2Space β]
    (f : α →+ β) (hf : Continuous f) {s : ℕ → Matrix m n α} (hs : Summable s) :
    (∑' k, s k).map f = ∑' k, (s k).map f

entries.name: Matrix.map_pow
entries.snippet:

    (f : α →+* β) (A : Matrix m m α) (k : ℕ) :
    (A ^ k).map f = (A.map f) ^ k

entries.name: NormedSpace.exp_map_algebraMap
entries.snippet:
lemma exp_map_algebraMap {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (A : Matrix n n ℝ) :
    (exp ℝ A).map (algebraMap ℝ ℂ) = exp ℂ (A.map (algebraMap ℝ ℂ))

entries.name: Matrix.det_exp_real
entries.docstring:
Lie's trace formula over ℝ: det(exp(A)) = exp(tr(A)) for any real matrix A.
This is proved by transferring the result from ℂ using the naturality of polynomial identities.
entries.snippet:
theorem det_exp_real {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [LinearOrder n]
    (A : Matrix n n ℝ) : (NormedSpace.exp ℝ A).det = Real.exp A.trace

lemma insert_filter_card_zero
    (T : Multiset (Charges 𝓩)) (S5 S10 : Finset 𝓩)
    (p : Charges 𝓩 → Prop) [DecidablePred p]
    (hComplet : ∀ x ∈ T, IsComplete x)
    (h10 : ∀ q10 : S10, ((T.map fun x => (x.1, x.2.1, x.2.2.1, insert q10.1 x.2.2.2)).filter
      fun y => (y ∉ T ∧ p y)) = ∅)
    (h5 : ∀ q5 : S5, ((T.map fun x => (x.1, x.2.1, insert q5.1 x.2.2.1, x.2.2.2)).filter

    (hnotSubset : ∀ (x y : Charges 𝓩), x ⊆ y → ¬ p x → ¬ p y)
    (hComplet : ∀ x ∈ T, IsComplete x)
    (x : Charges 𝓩)
    (hx : x ∈ T) (y : Charges 𝓩) (hsubset : x ⊆ y)
    (hy : y ∈ ofFinset S5 S10)
    (h10 : ∀ q10 : S10, ((T.map fun x => (x.1, x.2.1, x.2.2.1, insert q10.1 x.2.2.2)).filter
      fun y => (y ∉ T ∧ p y)) = ∅)
    (h5 : ∀ q5 : S5, ((T.map fun x => (x.1, x.2.1, insert q5.1 x.2.2.1, x.2.2.2)).filter
      fun y => (y ∉ T ∧ p y)) = ∅) :

    have hxy : x = y

entries.snippet:
lemma completeness_of_isPhenoClosedQ5_isPhenoClosedQ10
    {S5 S10 : Finset 𝓩} {charges : Multiset (Charges 𝓩)}
    (charges_topYukawa : ∀ x ∈ charges, x.AllowsTerm .topYukawa)
    (charges_not_isPhenoConstrained : ∀ x ∈ charges, ¬ x.IsPhenoConstrained)
    (charges_yukawa : ∀ x ∈ charges, ¬ x.YukawaGeneratesDangerousAtLevel 1)
    (charges_complete : ∀ x ∈ charges, x.IsComplete)
    (charges_isPhenoClosedQ5 : IsPhenoClosedQ5 S5 charges)
    (charges_isPhenoClosedQ10 : IsPhenoClosedQ10 S10 charges)
    (charges_exist : ContainsPhenoCompletionsOfMinimallyAllows S5 S10 charges)
    {x : Charges 𝓩} (hsub : x ∈ ofFinset S5 S10) :
    x ∈ charges ↔ AllowsTerm x .topYukawa ∧
    ¬ IsPhenoConstrained x ∧ ¬ YukawaGeneratesDangerousAtLevel x 1 ∧ IsComplete x

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.mathematicalPartitionFunction

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.differentialEntropy_nonneg_of_prob_le_one
entries.docstring:
General entropy non-negativity under a pointwise upper bound `probability ≤ 1`.
This assumption holds automatically in the finite/counting case (since sums bound each term),
but can fail in general (continuous) settings; hence we separate it as a hypothesis.
Finite case: see `CanonicalEnsemble.entropy_nonneg` in `Finite`.

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.helmholtzFreeEnergy

The Helmholtz free energy, `F = -k_B T log(Z)`. This is the central

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.helmholtzFreeEnergy_def

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.physicalProbability
entries.docstring:
The dimensionless physical probability density. This is is the probability density w.r.t. the
measure, obtained by dividing the phase space measure by the fundamental unit `h^dof`, making the
probability density `ρ_phys = ρ_math * h^dof` dimensionless.

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.physicalProbability_def
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma physicalProbability_def (T : Temperature) (i : ι) :

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.thermodynamicEntropy
entries.docstring:
The absolute thermodynamic entropy, defined from its statistical mechanical foundation as
the Gibbs-Shannon entropy of the dimensionless physical probability distribution.
This corresponds to Landau & Lifshitz, Statistical Physics, §7, Eq. 7.12.

entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma thermodynamicEntropy_def (T : Temperature) :
    𝓒.thermodynamicEntropy T = -kB * ∫ i, Real.log (𝓒.physicalProbability T i) ∂ 𝓒.μProd T

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.shannonEntropy
entries.docstring:
The Shannon entropy of a finite canonical ensemble.
This is defined by the formula `S = -k_B ∑ pᵢ log pᵢ`. It is proven to be
equivalent to the `differentialEntropy` and the `thermodynamicEntropy` for systems
satisfying the `IsFinite` property.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def shannonEntropy (T : Temperature) : ℝ

    𝓒.mathematicalPartitionFunction T = ∑ i, exp (- β T * 𝓒.energy i)

entries.snippet:
lemma probability_le_one [IsFinite 𝓒] [Nonempty ι] (T : Temperature) (i : ι) :

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.partitionFunction_pos_finite
entries.docstring: Finite specialization: strict positivity of the (physical) partition function.
entries.snippet:
lemma partitionFunction_pos_finite [IsFinite 𝓒] [Nonempty ι] (T : Temperature) :

entries.snippet:
lemma probability_nonneg_finite [IsFinite 𝓒] [Nonempty ι] (T : Temperature) (i : ι) :

    ∑ i, 𝓒.probability T i = 1

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.entropy_nonneg
entries.docstring: The entropy of a finite canonical ensemble (Shannon entropy) is non-negative.
entries.snippet:
lemma entropy_nonneg [IsFinite 𝓒] [Nonempty ι] (T : Temperature) :
    0 ≤ 𝓒.shannonEntropy T

lemma shannonEntropy_eq_differentialEntropy [IsFinite 𝓒] (T : Temperature) :

entries.docstring:
In the finite, nonempty case the thermodynamic and Shannon entropies coincide.
All semi-classical correction factors vanish (`dof = 0`, `phaseSpaceUnit = 1`),
so the absolute thermodynamic entropy reduces to the discrete Shannon form.
entries.snippet:
theorem thermodynamicEntropy_eq_shannonEntropy [IsFinite 𝓒]
    (T : Temperature) :
    𝓒.thermodynamicEntropy T = 𝓒.shannonEntropy T

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.mathematicalHelmholtzFreeEnergy
entries.docstring:
An intermediate potential defined from the mathematical partition function. See
`helmholtzFreeEnergy` for the physical thermodynamic quantity.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def mathematicalHelmholtzFreeEnergy (T : Temperature) : ℝ

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.helmholtzFreeEnergy_eq_helmholtzMathematicalFreeEnergy_add_correction
entries.docstring: The relationship between the physical Helmholtz Free Energy and the Helmholtz Potential.
entries.snippet:
lemma helmholtzFreeEnergy_eq_helmholtzMathematicalFreeEnergy_add_correction (T : Temperature)
    [IsFiniteMeasure (𝓒.μBolt T)] [NeZero 𝓒.μ] :
    𝓒.helmholtzFreeEnergy T = 𝓒.mathematicalHelmholtzFreeEnergy T +
      kB * T.val * 𝓒.dof * Real.log (𝓒.phaseSpaceunit)

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.differentialEntropy_eq_kB_beta_meanEnergy_add_kB_log_mathZ
entries.docstring:
General identity: S_diff = kB β ⟨E⟩ + kB log Z_math.
This connects the differential entropy to the mean energy and the mathematical partition function.
Integrability of `log (probability …)` follows from the pointwise formula.
entries.snippet:
lemma differentialEntropy_eq_kB_beta_meanEnergy_add_kB_log_mathZ
    (T : Temperature) [IsFiniteMeasure (𝓒.μBolt T)] [NeZero 𝓒.μ]
    (hE : Integrable 𝓒.energy (𝓒.μProd T)) :
    𝓒.differentialEntropy T = kB * (T.β : ℝ) * 𝓒.meanEnergy T +
      kB * Real.log (𝓒.mathematicalPartitionFunction T)

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.log_probability
entries.docstring: Pointwise logarithm of the Boltzmann probability.
entries.snippet:
lemma log_probability
    (𝓒 : CanonicalEnsemble ι) (T : Temperature)
    [IsFiniteMeasure (𝓒.μBolt T)] [NeZero 𝓒.μ] (i : ι) :
    Real.log (𝓒.probability T i)
      = - (β T) * 𝓒.energy i - Real.log (𝓒.mathematicalPartitionFunction T)

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.kB_mul_beta
entries.docstring:
Auxiliary identity: `kB · β = 1 / T`.
`β` is defined as `1 / (kB · T)` (see `Temperature.β`).

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.thermodynamicEntropy_eq_differentialEntropy_sub_correction
entries.docstring:
Fundamental relation between thermodynamic and differential entropy:
`S_thermo = S_diff - kB * dof * log h`.
entries.snippet:
lemma thermodynamicEntropy_eq_differentialEntropy_sub_correction
    (T : Temperature)
    (hE : Integrable 𝓒.energy (𝓒.μProd T))
    [IsFiniteMeasure (𝓒.μBolt T)] [NeZero 𝓒.μ] :
    𝓒.thermodynamicEntropy T
      = 𝓒.differentialEntropy T
        - kB * 𝓒.dof * Real.log 𝓒.phaseSpaceunit

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.thermodynamicEntropy_eq_differentialEntropy_of_dof_zero
entries.docstring: No semiclassical correction when `dof = 0`.
entries.snippet:
lemma thermodynamicEntropy_eq_differentialEntropy_of_dof_zero
    (T : Temperature) (hE : Integrable 𝓒.energy (𝓒.μProd T))
    (h0 : 𝓒.dof = 0)
    [IsFiniteMeasure (𝓒.μBolt T)] [NeZero 𝓒.μ] :
    𝓒.thermodynamicEntropy T = 𝓒.differentialEntropy T

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.thermodynamicEntropy_eq_differentialEntropy_of_phase_space_unit_one
entries.docstring: No semiclassical correction when `phase_space_unit = 1`.
entries.snippet:
lemma thermodynamicEntropy_eq_differentialEntropy_of_phase_space_unit_one
    (T : Temperature) (hE : Integrable 𝓒.energy (𝓒.μProd T))
    (h1 : 𝓒.phaseSpaceunit = 1)
    [IsFiniteMeasure (𝓒.μBolt T)] [NeZero 𝓒.μ] :
    𝓒.thermodynamicEntropy T = 𝓒.differentialEntropy T

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.helmholtzFreeEnergy_eq_meanEnergy_sub_temp_mul_thermodynamicEntropy
entries.docstring:
The Helmholtz free energy `F` is related to the mean energy `U` and the absolute
thermodynamic entropy `S` by the identity `F = U - TS`. This theorem shows that the
statistically-defined quantities in this framework correctly satisfy this principle of
thermodynamics.
entries.snippet:
theorem helmholtzFreeEnergy_eq_meanEnergy_sub_temp_mul_thermodynamicEntropy
    (T : Temperature) (hT : 0 < T.val)
    [IsFiniteMeasure (𝓒.μBolt T)] [NeZero 𝓒.μ]
    (hE : Integrable 𝓒.energy (𝓒.μProd T)) :
    𝓒.helmholtzFreeEnergy T
      = 𝓒.meanEnergy T - T.val * 𝓒.thermodynamicEntropy T

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.differentialEntropy_eq_meanEnergy_sub_helmholtz_div_temp_add_correction
entries.docstring:
**Theorem: Helmholtz identity with semi–classical correction term**.
Physical identity (always true for `T > 0`):
  (U - F)/T   = S_thermo
and:
  S_thermo = S_diff - kB * dof * log h.
Hence:
  S_diff = (U - F)/T + kB * dof * log h.
This theorem gives the correct relation for the (mathematical / differential) entropy.
(Removing the correction is only valid in normalized discrete cases
with `dof = 0` (or `phaseSpaceUnit = 1`).)
entries.snippet:
theorem differentialEntropy_eq_meanEnergy_sub_helmholtz_div_temp_add_correction
    (𝓒 : CanonicalEnsemble ι) (T : Temperature)
    [IsFiniteMeasure (𝓒.μBolt T)] [NeZero 𝓒.μ]
    (hT : 0 < T.val)
    (hE : Integrable 𝓒.energy (𝓒.μProd T)) :
    𝓒.differentialEntropy T
      = (𝓒.meanEnergy T - 𝓒.helmholtzFreeEnergy T) / T.val
        + kB * 𝓒.dof * Real.log 𝓒.phaseSpaceunit

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.differentialEntropy_eq_meanEnergy_sub_helmholtz_div_temp
entries.docstring:
Discrete / normalized specialization of the previous theorem.
If either `dof = 0` (no semiclassical correction) or `phaseSpaceUnit = 1`
(so `log h = 0`), the correction term vanishes and we recover the bare Helmholtz identity
for the (differential) entropy.
entries.snippet:
lemma differentialEntropy_eq_meanEnergy_sub_helmholtz_div_temp
    (𝓒 : CanonicalEnsemble ι) (T : Temperature)
    [IsFiniteMeasure (𝓒.μBolt T)] [NeZero 𝓒.μ]
    (hT : 0 < T.val)
    (hE : Integrable 𝓒.energy (𝓒.μProd T))
    (hNorm : 𝓒.dof = 0 ∨ 𝓒.phaseSpaceunit = 1) :
    𝓒.differentialEntropy T
      = (𝓒.meanEnergy T - 𝓒.helmholtzFreeEnergy T) / T.val

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.hasDerivWithinAt_log_comp
entries.docstring: Chain rule convenience lemma for `log ∘ f` on a set.

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.meanEnergy_eq_neg_deriv_log_mathZ_of_beta
entries.docstring:
The mean energy is the negative derivative of the logarithm of the
(mathematical) partition function with respect to β = 1/(kB T).
see: Tong (§1.3.2, §1.3.3), L&L (§31, implicitly, and §36)
Here the derivative is a `derivWithin` over `Set.Ioi 0`
since `β > 0`.
entries.snippet:
lemma meanEnergy_eq_neg_deriv_log_mathZ_of_beta
    (𝓒 : CanonicalEnsemble ι) (T : Temperature)
    (hT_pos : 0 < T.val) [IsFiniteMeasure (𝓒.μBolt T)] [NeZero 𝓒.μ]
    (h_deriv :
        HasDerivWithinAt
          (fun β : ℝ => ∫ i, Real.exp (-β * 𝓒.energy i) ∂ 𝓒.μ)
          (- ∫ i, 𝓒.energy i * Real.exp (-(T.β : ℝ) * 𝓒.energy i) ∂𝓒.μ)
          (Set.Ioi 0) (T.β : ℝ)) :
    𝓒.meanEnergy T =
      - (derivWithin
          (fun β : ℝ => Real.log (∫ i, Real.exp (-β * 𝓒.energy i) ∂𝓒.μ))
          (Set.Ioi 0) (T.β : ℝ))

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.log_phys_eq_log_math_sub_const_on_Ioi
entries.docstring:
Helper: equality (on `Set.Ioi 0`) between the β–parametrized logarithm of the
physical partition function and the β–parametrized logarithm of the *mathematical*
partition function up to the (β–independent) semiclassical correction. This is used only
to identify derivatives (the correction drops).
We add the hypothesis `h_fin` giving finiteness of the Boltzmann measure for every β > 0
(as needed to ensure the mathematical partition function is strictly positive).
entries.snippet:
private lemma log_phys_eq_log_math_sub_const_on_Ioi
    (𝓒 : CanonicalEnsemble ι) [NeZero 𝓒.μ]
    (h_fin :
      ∀ β > 0,
        IsFiniteMeasure (𝓒.μBolt (Temperature.ofβ (Real.toNNReal β))))
    (h_const :
        (𝓒.dof : ℝ) * Real.log 𝓒.phaseSpaceunit =
        (𝓒.dof : ℝ) * Real.log 𝓒.phaseSpaceunit := rfl) :
    Set.EqOn
      (fun β : ℝ =>
        Real.log (𝓒.partitionFunction (Temperature.ofβ (Real.toNNReal β))))
      (fun β : ℝ =>
        Real.log (∫ i, Real.exp (-β * 𝓒.energy i) ∂ 𝓒.μ)
          - (𝓒.dof : ℝ) * Real.log 𝓒.phaseSpaceunit)
      (Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ))

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.derivWithin_log_phys_eq_derivWithin_log_math
entries.docstring:
Derivative equality needed in `meanEnergy_eq_neg_deriv_log_Z_of_beta`.
Adds `h_fin` (finiteness of the Boltzmann measure for every β > 0).
entries.snippet:
private lemma derivWithin_log_phys_eq_derivWithin_log_math
    (𝓒 : CanonicalEnsemble ι) (T : Temperature)
    (hT_pos : 0 < T.val)
    [IsFiniteMeasure (𝓒.μBolt T)] [NeZero 𝓒.μ]
    (h_integrable :
        ∀ β > 0, Integrable (fun i => Real.exp (-β * 𝓒.energy i)) 𝓒.μ)
    (h_fin :
        ∀ β > 0,
          IsFiniteMeasure (𝓒.μBolt (Temperature.ofβ (Real.toNNReal β)))) :
    derivWithin
      (fun β : ℝ => Real.log (𝓒.partitionFunction (ofβ (Real.toNNReal β))))
      (Set.Ioi 0) (T.β : ℝ)
    =
    derivWithin
      (fun β : ℝ => Real.log (∫ i, Real.exp (-β * 𝓒.energy i) ∂ 𝓒.μ))
      (Set.Ioi 0) (T.β : ℝ)

entries.name: CanonicalEnsemble.meanEnergy_eq_neg_deriv_log_Z_of_beta
entries.docstring:
The mean energy can also be expressed as the negative derivative of the logarithm of the
*physical* partition function with respect to β. This follows from the fact that the physical and
mathematical partition functions differ only by a constant factor, which vanishes upon
differentiation.
entries.snippet:
theorem meanEnergy_eq_neg_deriv_log_Z_of_beta
    (𝓒 : CanonicalEnsemble ι) (T : Temperature)
    (hT_pos : 0 < T.val) [IsFiniteMeasure (𝓒.μBolt T)] [NeZero 𝓒.μ]
    (h_integrable :
        ∀ β > 0, Integrable (fun i => Real.exp (-β * 𝓒.energy i)) 𝓒.μ)
    (h_fin :
        ∀ β > 0,
          IsFiniteMeasure (𝓒.μBolt (Temperature.ofβ (Real.toNNReal β))))
    (h_deriv :
        HasDerivWithinAt
          (fun β : ℝ => ∫ i, Real.exp (-β * 𝓒.energy i) ∂ 𝓒.μ)
          (- ∫ i, 𝓒.energy i * Real.exp (-(T.β : ℝ) * 𝓒.energy i) ∂𝓒.μ)
          (Set.Ioi 0) (T.β : ℝ)) :
    𝓒.meanEnergy T =
      - (derivWithin
          (fun β : ℝ => Real.log (𝓒.partitionFunction (ofβ (Real.toNNReal β))))
          (Set.Ioi 0) (T.β : ℝ))

    (S.map (fun x => (0, |x.1 + x.2|))).sum = S.sum

entries.docstring:
The quanta associated with the representations in a `SU(5) x U(1)` F-theory.

  `Hu` particles (there values of `(M,N)` are not included as they are

entries.name: FTheory.SU5.Quanta.AnomalyCancellation
entries.docstring:
The anomaly cancellation conditions on quanta making up the fields present in
  the theory. This corresponds to the conditions that:

- `∑ᵢ qᵢ Nᵢ + ∑ₐ qₐ Nₐ = 0` where the first sum is over all 5-bar represenations and the second
  is over all 10d representations.
- `∑ᵢ qᵢ² Nᵢ + 3 * ∑ₐ qₐ² Nₐ = 0` where the first sum is over all 5-bar represenations and the
  second is over all 10d representations.
entries.snippet:
def AnomalyCancellation [CommRing 𝓩] (qHd qHu : Option 𝓩) (F : FiveQuanta 𝓩) (T : TenQuanta 𝓩) :
    Prop

entries.name: FTheory.SU5.Quanta.«instance@d2931221»
entries.snippet:
instance [CommRing 𝓩] [DecidableEq 𝓩] :
    Decidable (AnomalyCancellation (𝓩 := 𝓩) qHd qHu F T)

entries.name: FTheory.SU5.Quanta.anomalyCoefficent_snd_eq_zero_of_anomalyCancellation
entries.snippet:
lemma anomalyCoefficent_snd_eq_zero_of_anomalyCancellation [CommRing 𝓩]
    {qHd qHu : Option 𝓩} {F : FiveQuanta 𝓩} {T : TenQuanta 𝓩}
    (h : AnomalyCancellation qHd qHu F T) :
    ((HdAnomalyCoefficent qHd).2 + (HuAnomalyCoefficent qHu).2
    + (F.anomalyCoefficent).2 + (T.anomalyCoefficent).2) = 0

entries.name: FTheory.SU5.Quanta.isViable_iff_expand_ofFinset
entries.snippet:
lemma isViable_iff_expand_ofFinset (I : CodimensionOneConfig) (x : Quanta) :
    IsViable I x ↔
      x.toCharges.IsComplete ∧
  ¬ x.toCharges.IsPhenoConstrained ∧
  ¬ x.toCharges.YukawaGeneratesDangerousAtLevel 1 ∧
  AllowsTerm x.toCharges topYukawa ∧
  x.2.2.1.toFluxesFive.NoExotics ∧
  x.2.2.1.toFluxesFive.HasNoZero ∧
  x.2.2.2.toFluxesTen.NoExotics ∧
  x.2.2.2.toFluxesTen.HasNoZero ∧
  AnomalyCancellation x.1 x.2.1 x.2.2.1 x.2.2.2 ∧
  (x.1.toFinset ⊆ I.allowedBarFiveCharges ∧ x.2.1.toFinset ⊆ I.allowedBarFiveCharges ∧
      x.toCharges.2.2.1 ⊆ I.allowedBarFiveCharges ∧ x.toCharges.2.2.2 ⊆ I.allowedTenCharges)
      ∧
    x.2.2.1.toCharges.Nodup ∧
    x.2.2.2.toCharges.Nodup

entries.name: UnitChoices.dimScale
entries.docstring:

  element of `ℝ≥0` corresponding to the scaling (by definition) of a quantity of dimension `d`

entries.name: UnitDependent
entries.docstring:
A type carries the instance `UnitDependent M` if it depends on a choice of units.
  This dependence is manifested in `scaleUnit u1 u2` which describes how elements of `M` change
  under a scaling of units which would take `u1` to `u2`.

  This type is used for functions, and propositions etc.
entries.snippet:
class UnitDependent (M : Type) where
  scaleUnit : UnitChoices → UnitChoices → M → M
  scaleUnit_trans : ∀ u1 u2 u3 m, scaleUnit u2 u3 (scaleUnit u1 u2 m) = scaleUnit u1 u3 m
  scaleUnit_trans' : ∀ u1 u2 u3 m, scaleUnit u1 u2 (scaleUnit u2 u3 m) = scaleUnit u1 u3 m
  scaleUnit_id : ∀ u m, scaleUnit u u m = m

entries.name: MulUnitDependent
entries.docstring:
A type `M` with an instance of `UnitDependent M` such that `scaleUnit u1 u2` is compatible
  with the `MulAction ℝ≥0 M` instance on `M`.
entries.snippet:
class MulUnitDependent (M : Type) [MulAction ℝ≥0 M] extends
    UnitDependent M where
  scaleUnit_mul : ∀ u1 u2 (r : ℝ≥0) m,
    scaleUnit u1 u2 (r • m) = r • scaleUnit u1 u2 m

entries.name: LinearUnitDependent
entries.docstring:
A type `M` with an instance of `UnitDependent M` such that `scaleUnit u1 u2` is compatible
  with the `Module ℝ M` instance on `M`.
entries.snippet:
class LinearUnitDependent (M : Type) [AddCommMonoid M] [Module ℝ M] extends UnitDependent M where
  scaleUnit_add : ∀ u1 u2 m1 m2,
    scaleUnit u1 u2 (m1 + m2) = scaleUnit u1 u2 m1 + scaleUnit u1 u2 m2
  scaleUnit_smul : ∀ u1 u2 (r : ℝ) m,
    scaleUnit u1 u2 (r • m) = r • scaleUnit u1 u2 m

entries.name: ContinuousLinearUnitDependent
entries.docstring:
A type `M` with an instance of `UnitDependent M` such that `scaleUnit u1 u2` is compatible
  with the `Module ℝ M` instance on `M`, and is continuous.
entries.snippet:
class ContinuousLinearUnitDependent (M : Type) [AddCommMonoid M] [Module ℝ M]
    [TopologicalSpace M] extends LinearUnitDependent M where
  scaleUnit_cont : ∀ u1 u2, Continuous (scaleUnit u1 u2)

entries.snippet:

entries.name: IsDimensionallyInvariant
entries.docstring:
A term of type `M` carrying an instance of `UnitDependent M` is said to be
  dimensionally invariant if under a change of units it remains the same.

  This corresponds to the statement that term is dimensionally correct.

entries.name: isDimensionallyInvariant_iff

    IsDimensionallyInvariant m ↔ ∀ u1 u2 : UnitChoices,
      scaleUnit u1 u2 m = m

entries.name: integral_isDimensionallyInvariant
entries.docstring:
The statement that for a measure `μ` of dimension `d`, and a function
  `f : M → G` of dimension `(CarriesDimension.d G * d⁻¹)` (where `CarriesDimension.d G`
  is the dimension associated with terms of type `G`), then
  `∫ x, f x ∂μ `
  has the correct dimension, namely `CarriesDimension.d G`.

  In other words, the function:
```
fun (μ : DimSet (MeasureTheory.Measure M) d)
    (f : DimSet (M → G) (CarriesDimension.d G * d⁻¹)) ↦ ∫ x, f.1 x ∂μ.1
```
  is dimensionally invariant.
entries.snippet:
lemma integral_isDimensionallyInvariant (d : Dimension) :
    IsDimensionallyInvariant (fun (μ : DimSet (MeasureTheory.Measure M) d)
      (f : DimSet (M → G) (CarriesDimension.d G * d⁻¹)) ↦ ∫ x, f.1 x ∂μ.1)
